summary.text: At \(n=7\), every permitted value of \(x\) is at least \(3\); since \(x\le y\le z\), this forces \(x+y+z\ge 3x\ge 9\), contradicting the required sum of \(7\).

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
S=\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
The conjecture is a conjunction of two assertions for every natural number \(n\):

1. if \(n>5\), then \(a(n)>0\), where \(a(n)\) counts ordered-by-size positive triples \(x\le y\le z\) with \(x+y+z=n\) for which
\[
2x-1,\quad 2y-1,\quad 2z-1,\quad 2xy-1,\quad 2xz-1,\quad 2yz-1
\]
are all prime; and

2. if \(n>6\), then there is such a positive triple \(x\le y\le z\) with the additional condition \(x\in S\).

We disprove the second assertion at \(n=7\). Since \(7>6\), the conjecture would provide natural numbers \(x,y,z\) satisfying
\[
x>0,\qquad y>0,\qquad z>0,
\]
\[
x+y+z=7,
\]
\[
x\le y\le z,
\]
and
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\},
\]
as well as all six primality conditions. We will obtain a contradiction before the primality conditions are even relevant.

Membership in the displayed finite set gives the exhaustive alternatives
\[
x=3,\quad x=4,\quad x=6,\quad x=10,\quad\text{or}\quad x=15.
\]
In every case, \(x\ge 3\). Because \(x\le y\), we have \(y\ge x\ge3\). Also, from \(x\le y\le z\), transitivity gives \(x\le z\), so \(z\ge x\ge3\). Consequently,
\[
x+y+z\ge 3+3+3=9.
\]
Equivalently, one may add the inequalities \(x\le y\) and \(x\le z\) to obtain
\[
x+y+z\ge x+x+x=3x\ge9.
\]
This contradicts the required equality \(x+y+z=7\).

Thus no positive ordered triple \(x\le y\le z\) summing to \(7\) can have its least entry \(x\) in \(\{3,4,6,10,15\}\). In particular, no such triple can satisfy the additional six primality requirements. Hence the “moreover” implication is false for \(n=7\).

The original statement universally asserts, for each \(n\), the conjunction of the positivity claim for \(a(n)\) and this additional representation claim. A conjunction is false if either conjunct is false. Therefore the failure of the additional representation claim at \(n=7\) disproves the entire conjecture, independently of whether \(a(7)>0\).
